items: Fundamental Rights available ONLY to Indian citizens (denied to foreigners): Articles 15, 16, 19, 29, and 30.
In India, both a natural-born citizen as well as a naturalised citizen are eligible for the office of President, whereas in the USA, only a natural-born citizen is eligible.
Article 11 empowers Parliament to enact laws on citizenship, leading to the enactment of the Citizenship Act, 1955.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Part II of the Constitution of India (Articles 5 to 11) deals with Citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution.
The Citizenship Act of 1955 provides five modes to acquire citizenship: Birth, Descent, Registration, Naturalisation, and Incorporation of Territory.
The Citizenship Act of 1955 details three modes of losing citizenship: Renunciation, Termination, and Deprivation.
Article 11 explicitly grants Parliament the exclusive power to regulate rights of citizenship by law.
India provides for Single Citizenship for the entire country to foster national integration and harmony.
